title: Sneaking in to hear Frank Dusen's band and Picou
summary: As a boy of twelve he slipped into Odd Fellows Hall to hear Dusen's band, dressed in tall hats, and a new clarinetist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: So how does Bolton fit into this?

Now, let me show you. Well, Frank Deucin. I was a kid, right to separation from the hall to my house, in a big picket fence. So I and a bunch of boys hanging around the corner. How old were you? Huh? Oh, around about 12. So, me living next to the hall. The fellow used to run it. Called him, uh, John Shailis. He was a manager. So I'd ask him. I said, John said, let me sweep up the hall. All right, you sweep up the hall. And in the night time, he'd leave me going in the hall. So I'd take him down about two or three pickets off the fence in the back. And I'd have about four or five of my little friends. When the ball was start, we'd go through the back door, sneak in, you know. We'd get in the ball, look at the fellas, play. That's about the first time I ever saw Piku. Now, Frank's Houston band, Frank had himself. He had a trumpet player named Ned. And he had a clarinet player named Frank Lewis. And, uh, he had a drum player. They called him, uh, Jimmy Phillips. He was thinking of his band now. And they had a peg-legged fella. They called him Ike. He played bass. All right. So they played there. One night, I see him come over, Frank Lewis. He was sick. And it was announcing Frank, he lived in Algea, announcing about the fella he was going to have play, one of the best clarinet players in the town he was going to have with him. So the people was anxious to see that clarinet player.
They wear their hats, never take their hat off.
They didn't take their hats off?
No. Frank Deucem? No. He go play in your parlor. There's a big old high roller hat on.
What kind of hat? Big old high roller, man.
He used to wear a high roller hat. Big old high roller like a... Stove pipe? Yeah, stove pipe. Big old silk hanker around his neck.
Is it just Doosan or all the members of his band?
Well, all of them wear their hats.

Yeah, but Frank, he was the ratty one, you know. Had his parents all on, buttoned in the front. He had suspenders on. His parents would whip him out of his waist. Big silk hanker. Big old studsion hat on his head. Uh-huh. Well, that night, that dance, everybody was saying, who that new clandette player? Yes, there was, go now, see a fella up in there. You know, he's very bright. Big old. He had a lot of hair. He had a big old champagne color, stuffed in a wide hat like a cardboard hat. Blue eyes, you know. Oh, gee, the people's womb. You got a white man playing with him. He had good hair? Sure, they're fine hair. Fine, black hair. Very bright. Blue eyes. Well, all right. All they found, he was a great clandette player. So, well, after Frank got well, this really clandette player, Frank Lewis, he came home again. Well, Frankie Dooson. Buddy Bowling hired Frankie Dooson now. What about Frankie Dooson so good now, Jeds? He had a ratted trombone player, you know. Val. Well, Buddy had his band, Bowling Band. He had a Willie Carnish, a big trombone player then. He had a drummer with D.D. Channel. Guitar player. Brock Mumford. Slim Colton had a barber shop. Trying to think of Buddy's, all Buddy's men.
